title: Committee Of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee Of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Drop in ranking
sections.summary: This year the ranking dropped to eighth position from fourth position a year before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Disappointingly, this year, we have dropped to eighth position from fourth position a year before.

sections.label: Task force progress update
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can provide an update on the task force's progress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress of this task force?

sections.label: High-sugar drinks consultation
sections.summary: MOH sought views on four proposals for prepacked high-sugar drinks and the passage asks if a decision was reached.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: From December last year till January this year, MOH sought views on four proposals: (a) a total ban on prepacked high-sugar drinks; (b) single or tiered taxes on high-sugar drinks; (c) mandatory front-of-pack labelling on sugar/nutrition content; and finally, perhaps even (d) a ban on advertisements for high-sugar drinks on all platforms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Has a decision been reached following the public consultation on possible measures for prepackaged sugar-sweetened beverages?

sections.label: Alcohol consumption limit review
sections.summary: The passage states MOH's recommended alcohol limits and says the recommendation should be reviewed given findings of no safe level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MOH’s current recommended limit for regular alcohol consumption is two standard drinks a day for men and one standard drink a day for women.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should review this recommendation in view of the latest findings that there is, in fact, no safe level of alcohol consumption.

sections.label: Overweight rates in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage gives projected overweight percentages for 2025 and 2017 MOH figures for Singaporeans and children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the percentages of overweight men and women are expected to increase to 36.5% and 21.7% respectively by 2025, according to the World Obesity Federation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2017, MOH figures showed that 36.2% of Singaporeans aged 18 to 69 years and 13% of children in mainstream schools are overweight.

sections.label: Screen for Life and immunisation
sections.summary: The passage describes the Screen for Life programme, MediSave use for vaccinations, and the National Adult Immunisation Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Screen for Life (SFL) programme is a landmark initiative as early disease detection typically supersedes any medical treatment for established diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since November 2017, adult Singaporeans can now use their MediSave to pay for vaccinations which MOH is recommending depending on their age and health status.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The new National Adult Immunisation Schedule, which lists who should be vaccinated and when, includes immunisation for diseases, such as the flu and hepatitis B.

sections.label: New models of care
sections.summary: The passage calls for more ambulatory, community, home-based, stepdown and intermediate care, and wider preventive services, for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The second area is really to embark on new models of care.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This must be more in terms of ambulatory, more community-based, more home-based care, more stepdown care and more intermediate care needs as we move forward with an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There will also be a need to review more preventive services and to have these made more widely available and accessible.

sections.label: Healthcare productivity and LEAP update
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister about healthcare productivity, how targets are set, and progress of the regulatory sandbox licensing LEAP programme.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With all that in mind, I would like to ask Minister: first, on our healthcare productivity, how are we doing and how are our targets set and how are we moving ahead with this?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thirdly, can we also have an update on the progress of the regulatory sandbox licensing experimentation and adoption programme (LEAP).

sections.label: MediShield Life coverage change
sections.summary: A change in MediShield Life coverage will help residents pay for these cares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A change in MediShield Life coverage will help residents in paying for these "cares".

sections.label: SCDF and private ambulances
sections.summary: SCDF ambulances attend about 90% of emergency cases, while consumers call private ambulances for preferred or private hospitals and non-emergency cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, while the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) ambulances attend to about 90% of emergency cases, consumers will call for private ambulances in emergency cases if they wish to send a patient to a preferred or private hospital and in non-emergency cases.

sections.label: Cash-only business payments
sections.summary: Some businesses take cash payments only, which can be stressful when charges reach about $1,000 paid by a family at night.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some businesses insist on taking cash payments only, which can be stressful if the charges come up to about $1,000 to be paid by the family in the middle of the night.

sections.label: Ambulance licensing distinction concern
sections.summary: One concern is the proposed distinction in licensing requirements between emergency ambulance services and medical transport services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One concern is the proposed distinction in licensing requirements between those operating emergency ambulance services and those operating medical transport services.

sections.label: MOH regulation review and fee benchmarks
sections.summary: Asks about the status of MOH's review of the regulation regime and whether the Government will publish fee benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the status of MOH's review of the regulation regime?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for the reasonableness of the charges, will the Government consider publishing fee benchmarks so as to keep this essential service affordable?

sections.label: Precision medicine strategy update
sections.summary: The Minister replied that the Ministry was developing an integrated national strategy for precision medicine research and implementation and would update later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister replied that the Ministry was developing an integrated national strategy for precision medicine research and implementation and would provide a thorough update at an appropriate time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask for an update.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There have been reports that hundreds of patients have benefited from personalised medicine treatments at our public hospitals.

sections.label: Gene-edited baby experiment
sections.summary: Last November, a Chinese scientist used gene-editing technology in an experiment that led to the birth of the world's first genetically modified baby.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, last November, a Chinese scientist used gene-editing technology in an experiment that led to the birth of the world’s first genetically modified baby.

sections.label: 2018 NEHR public sentiments survey
sections.summary: A 2018 joint survey showed over 11% of respondents would prefer to opt out of NEHR and 56% wanted records kept without provider access absent explicit consent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, a joint survey on public sentiments towards NEHR showed that over 11% of respondents said they would prefer to opt out of NEHR and 56% said they would like to have their records maintained in NEHR but do not want any healthcare provider to access it without their explicit consent except during emergencies.

sections.label: Primary care providers entering NEHR notes
sections.summary: MOH announced that primary care providers, such as private GPs, will be required to enter case notes into NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: MOH has announced that primary care providers, such as private GPs, will be required to enter case notes into NEHR.

sections.label: Sensitivity of patient data
sections.summary: Patient data is often, and sometimes very, sensitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, patient data is often – and sometimes very – sensitive.

sections.label: Three pillars of healthcare financing
sections.summary: MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund are the three pillars of public healthcare financing supporting all Singaporeans' healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund are the three pillars of our public healthcare financing system supporting the healthcare needs of all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Public healthcare expenditure doubled
sections.summary: Public healthcare expenditure has more than doubled within five to six years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Objectively, we know that public healthcare expenditure has more than doubled within a short span of five to six years.

sections.label: MediSave draw for long-term care
sections.summary: From 2020, severely disabled Singaporeans may draw up to $200 a month from MediSave for long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Chairman, from 2020, severely disabled Singaporeans will be allowed to draw up to $200 a month from MediSave for long-term care needs.

sections.label: MediSave limit versus nursing home stay
sections.summary: The $200 limit is prime for 100 months, while the median nursing home stay is 59 months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: The current limit of $200 is prime for 100 months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: However, the median duration of stay in a nursing home is 59 months.

sections.label: ElderShield premiums and payouts
sections.summary: From 2002 to 2016 ElderShield collected $2.6 billion in premiums and paid out slightly over $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the pain points that was manifested through public discussions prior to the debate in this House on the CareShield Life White Paper last year surrounded the fact that from 2002 to 2016, ElderShield collected $2.6 billion in premiums, and only slightly in excess of $100 million was paid out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The importance of pre-funding for such schemes aside, a general lack of understanding contributed to the public dissonance on the issue, as the numbers suggest over-collection of premiums.

sections.label: Question on MediShield Life premiums
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Council foresees a premium increase given ending transitional subsidies and loss ratios exceeding 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share, in light of MediShield Life transitional subsidies ending this year and the incurred loss ratios over the years exceeding 90% so far, does the Council foresee an increase in premiums in the near future?

sections.label: IP rider co-payment review
sections.summary: MOH was reviewing serious pregnancy and delivery complications, and from 1 April 2019 new IP riders must include at least 5% co-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: MOH said then that a review was being conducted for serious pregnancy and delivery complications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Could MOH provide an update on the review, please?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, from 1 April 2019, Singaporeans who purchase new IP riders will no longer be able to purchase "full-rider" policies and must be prepared for co-payment of at least 5% of the medical bill.

sections.label: Private in-patient bill increases
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported private sector average total in-patient bills rose 9% yearly from 2007 to 2017, nearly double the 4.9% public A Class rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Straits Times reported that the average total in-patient bill in the private sector has increased by 9% each year over the last 10 years, from 2007 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is almost double the 4.9% increase for bills in the public sector's A Class wards.

sections.label: CareShield Life participation incentive
sections.summary: The package includes a $1,500 participation incentive to join CareShield Life, on top of the previously announced $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: In particular, I note that the package includes a participation incentive of $1,500 to join CareShield Life on top of the previously announced $2,500.

sections.label: CareShield Life payouts and disciplinary review
sections.summary: Affected seniors get lifelong CareShield Life payouts versus six years under ElderShield400, and questions were raised on disciplinary processes and a pending review.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Affected seniors covered under CareShield Life will qualify for lifelong payouts, compared to only six years for the previous ElderShield400 system, and this will be very useful for paying for care assistance or necessary consumables.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I have several questions and suggestions on how these disciplinary processes currently operate and what would be the parameters governing the pending review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I understand that MOH has signalled its intent to do away with this avenue of appeal in future.

sections.label: SMC legal fees and premiums
sections.summary: It asks what measures minimise SMC legal fees for DTs paid by insurers, which could raise doctors' medical indemnity insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What measures are being taken to minimise the legal fees incurred by the SMC for DTs which are paid by insurers, since this has the potential to elevate medical indemnity insurance premiums borne by doctors?

sections.label: Healthcare Manpower Plan 2020
sections.summary: The Government's Healthcare Manpower Plan 2020, released in October 2016, estimated an addition of 30,000 healthcare workers by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the Government's Healthcare Manpower Plan 2020, released in October 2016, the healthcare services estimated an addition of 30,000 healthcare workers by 2020.

sections.label: Nursing manpower and local graduates
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry monitors enrolment and local graduate figures to reinforce and retain nursing manpower, noting local graduates fell from 1,744 in 2012 to 1,479 in 2015 and a 2017 statement that the foreign nursing workforce is 33%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How is the Ministry monitoring and ensuring that enrolment figures and local graduate figures translate into reinforcements to the nursing manpower, and then retaining the local graduates to meet the long-term plan of building a strong local workforce?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask as the number of local nursing graduates have been gradually decreasing since a peak of 1,744 graduates in 2012, to 1,479 graduates in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During the COS debate in 2017, Dr Amy Khor stated that the foreign workforce for nursing is 33%.

sections.label: VWOs in ILTC sector
sections.summary: The passage states that voluntary welfare organizations figure prominently in the Intermediate and Long-Term Care sector and that it is in our interest to ensure they flourish long term and become sources of good quality care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Voluntary welfare organizations (VWOs) figure prominently in the Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It is in our interest to ensure that these VWOs flourish in the long term and become sources of good quality care.

sections.label: Private sector investment in ILTC
sections.summary: The passage states capacity-building is one area where VWOs may face challenges, that the VWO sector may need augmentation by the private sector, and asks what the Government is doing to engage and support good companies to invest and partner VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Capacity-building is one area where VWOs may face challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Lastly, in growing the ILTC sector, the VWO sector may need to be augmented by the private sector, which has potentially a substantial capacity to invest financially, as well as, in some cases, to deploy relevant, cutting-edge technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What is the Government doing to engage and support good companies to invest in this sector and possibly to partner our VWOs?

sections.label: Life expectancy increases
sections.summary: The passage states life expectancy at birth rose from 83.2 years in 2010 to 84.8 years in 2017, and Health Adjusted Life Expectancy at birth rose from 72.9 to 74.2 years over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our life expectancy at birth has risen from 83.2 years in 2010 to 84.8 years in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Health Adjusted Life Expectancy at birth also increased from 72.9 years to 74.2 years over the same period.

sections.label: Chronic disease prevalence rates
sections.summary: The passage states that from 2010 to 2017 prevalence rates of diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia among Singapore residents aged 18 to 69 increased by 4%, 14% and 33% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: From 2010 to 2017, the prevalence rates of diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia among Singapore residents aged 18 to 69 have increased by 4%, 14% and 33% respectively.

sections.label: National healthcare expenditure growth
sections.summary: The passage states that since 2010 Singapore's national healthcare expenditure almost doubled from $11 billion to $21 billion in 2016, while Government Health Expenditure increased 2.4 times from $3.9 billion to $9.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Since 2010, Singapore’s national healthcare expenditure has almost doubled, from $11 billion to reach $21 billion in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Government Health Expenditure increased even faster, by 2.4 times, from $3.9 billion to $9.3 billion.

sections.label: IGH model phases one and two
sections.summary: About 4,000 patients benefited from Phase 1 of the IGH model, and MOHT and NUHS have commenced Phase 2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: About 4,000 patients have benefited from Phase 1 of the IGH model, which focuses primarily on inpatient care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: While efforts under Phase 1 will continue, MOHT and NUHS have commenced Phase 2, which aims to better integrate hospital care with community services required by patients living around Queentown.

sections.label: Regular security audits and penetration tests
sections.summary: Regular security audits are conducted, with the most recent penetration test done in October last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Regular security audits are conducted, with the most recent penetration test done in October last year.

sections.label: NEHR access logging and audits
sections.summary: All NEHR accesses are logged and subjected to monthly audits using analytics to detect unusual usage patterns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: All NEHR accesses are logged and subjected to monthly audits, using analytics to detect unusual usage patterns.

sections.label: Launch of MGP this year
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced in his Budget speech that the MGP will be launched this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As our Minister for Finance has announced in his Budget speech, we will be launching the MGP this year.

sections.label: National Value-based Healthcare Workgroup
sections.summary: Since 2017 MOH has appointed a National Value-based Healthcare Workgroup to compare clinical quality indicators and cost data across public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Since 2017, MOH has appointed a National Value-based Healthcare (NVH) Workgroup to look into this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: By comparing standardised clinical quality indicators and cost data across our public healthcare institutions, it will help our healthcare providers to identify best practices among them as well as identify opportunities to improve clinical outcomes in a cost-effective way.

sections.label: Stepped-up efforts on diabetes
sections.summary: In the year ahead efforts will be stepped up on diabetes, including recommending non-fasting screening and making early screening more convenient for women with gestational diabetes history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the year ahead, we will step up our efforts on several fronts, reducing diabetes-related amputations, empowering patients and healthcare professionals to better manage diabetes and minimise complications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In particular, we are also recommending the use of non-fasting screening test for diabetes to increase screening rates, and will make early screening more convenient for women with a history of gestational diabetes.

sections.label: Smoking deaths and social cost
sections.summary: Over 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely yearly from smoking-related diseases, and smoking's social cost is estimated at least $600 million annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: More than 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases each year, and the social cost of smoking in Singapore has been estimated to be at least $600 million annually.

sections.label: Seniors' disability and long-term care
sections.summary: MOH estimates one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 could become severely disabled, and about 83,000 individuals in 2030 will have ADL deficits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOH estimates that one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 could become severely disabled in their lifetime and may need long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: About 7% of the population or about 83,000 individuals in 2030 will have deficit in one or more ADLs.

sections.label: Ageing Gracefully @ Home expansion
sections.summary: The Ageing Gracefully @ Home programme by full-time shared caregivers including nurses should be expanded, especially at HDB rental blocks, providing home visits and services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For frail seniors, the Ageing Gracefully @ Home (AGH) programme carried out by full-time shared caregivers that include nurses should be expanded, especially at HDB rental blocks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under AGH, home visits are provided for these frail seniors with the following services: daily supervision on meals, blood pressure checks, medicine intake, home cleaning services, bathing, identifying people who are sick, medical assistance, hospital transportation and so on.

sections.label: Seniors living alone by 2030
sections.summary: The number of seniors living alone will double to about 92,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The number of seniors who will live alone will double to about to 92,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Subsidised private homecare providers
sections.summary: The Lien Foundation reported that as of 2018 only two of 60 private providers received subsidies with mandatory minimum MOH requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Lien Foundation reported that, as of 2018, only two out of 60 such private providers were receiving subsidies which came with mandatory minimum requirements by MOH.

sections.label: Regulating private homecare services
sections.summary: Questions ask what plans MOH has to regulate private homecare and centre-based services and ensure quality given absent mandatory minimum standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What plans does MOH have to regulate private homecare and centre-based services?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the absence of mandatory minimum service standards, what is being done to ensure the quality and effectiveness of these services?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credits for seniors
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government will consider a special top-up to SkillsFuture Credits for earnest senior learners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: As such, for the earnest senior learners, will the Government consider a special top-up to the SkillsFuture Credits for seniors?

sections.label: Seniors ageing successfully
sections.summary: The study revealed that 25.4% of seniors have aged successfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The study revealed that 25.4% of our seniors have aged successfully.

sections.label: Caregiver Support Action Plan measures
sections.summary: The Ministry introduced the Caregiver Support Action Plan with assistance such as the Home Caregiving Grant and night respite service, though financial burden can exceed the grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: For a long time, the Government was focused on addressing the direct needs of our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: But I am heartened that in the Parliamentary debate on caregivers just last month, the Ministry responded very encouragingly with the introduction of the Caregiver Support Action Plan, comprising assistance, such as the Home Caregiving Grant and night respite service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: I have no doubt that these assistance measures will alleviate the burden and stress caregivers face at present.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: However, as we know from our ground experiences, the financial burden on a caregiver who has given up her job can be significant, higher than what the caregiving grant can offer on a monthly basis.

sections.label: Engaging caregivers and accelerating plan
sections.summary: The question asks if the Ministry will continue engaging caregivers and accelerate the action plan so more caregivers benefit sooner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask the Ministry if it will continue to engage caregivers to ensure that their needs are understood and that the support put in place will address them adequately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also work towards accelerating the implementation of the action plan so that more caregivers can benefit sooner than later?

sections.label: Training and support resources
sections.summary: The passage asks what kinds of training caregivers can attend and what resources are available for emotional and psychological support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: For example, what kinds of training can they attend to carry out procedures which they may need to execute and what resources are available to them to provide emotional and psychological support?

sections.label: Measures for caregivers of seniors
sections.summary: During the debate on the Caregivers for Seniors' Motion, the Government announced measures including a $200 monthly Home Caregiver Grant and caregiver support network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: During the recent debate on the Caregivers for Seniors' Motion introduced in this House by hon Member of Parliament, Dr Chia Shi-Lu, the Government announced a slew of measures to help caregivers of seniors, such as provision of the Home Caregiver Grant of $200 per month and caregiver support network.

sections.label: Workplace stress survey findings
sections.summary: A 2017 Willis Towers Watson study found 44% of local employers named stress their top health issue and 60% of employees reported above average or high stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A 2017 study by Willis Towers Watson found that 44% of local employers identified stress as their No 1 health issue, while 60% of the employees admitted to having above average or high levels of stress.

sections.label: Unwillingness to discuss mental health
sections.summary: A 2018 NCSS survey found over half of those surveyed were unwilling to live or work with a person with a mental health condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many are unwilling to openly talk about such issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And a 2018 survey conducted by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) revealed that over half of those surveyed were unwilling to live or work with a person with a mental health condition.

sections.label: Abortion gestational age threshold question
sections.summary: The speaker first asked in 2014 whether the Ministry would consider adjusting the abortion gestational age threshold from 24 weeks to 22 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I first asked in 2014 if the Ministry will consider adjusting the threshold of gestational age for abortion from 24 weeks to 22 weeks, based on the increasing viability of even extreme preterm babies.

sections.label: Request to review gestational limit
sections.summary: The speaker repeats the request for the Ministry to carefully consider, based on medical evidence, whether the gestational limit should be reviewed and adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And I do hope that the unborn children of Singapore will truly find it a palace for them to develop well and a place of mercy for them who do not have a voice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, repeat my request for the Ministry's careful consideration, based on medical evidence, if a review of the gestational limit is due and an adjustment to the term limit be adopted.

sections.label: MOH public consultation on Action Plan
sections.summary: MOH will hold a public consultation later this year with stakeholders, including seniors, community and business partners, to develop an updated Action Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MOH will conduct a public consultation later this year with stakeholders, including seniors, community and business partners, to develop an updated Action Plan.

sections.label: Silver Generation Ambassadors engagement
sections.summary: Since early 2018, about 3,000 Silver Generation Ambassadors have engaged around 280,000 seniors, identifying needs and linking them to services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since the beginning of 2018, about 3,000 Silver Generation Ambassadors (SGAs) have engaged around 280,000 seniors, identifying seniors with needs and working with stakeholders to link them to active ageing, befriending and care services.

sections.label: MOH regulation and senior centres
sections.summary: MOH will review formal regulation, starting with licensing home medical services, and oversees 127 SACs, 118 SCCs and five AAHs as of end 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, MOH will review the need for more formal regulation, including licensing under the proposed Healthcare Services Bill, as Mr Louis Ng has also asked in a PQ.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will adopt a risk-based approach, and subject services with higher patient risks to higher levels of regulation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Hence, we will start with licensing home medical services, and review the need to license other services as the sector evolves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Following the transfer of functions from MSF, as of end 2018, MOH oversees 127 SACs providing wellness programmes to seniors living in studio apartments and rental flats; 118 Senior Care Centres (SCCs) providing daycare and community rehabilitation services, and five Active Ageing Hubs (AAHs) serving seniors across a spectrum of needs.

sections.label: Preventive health and community nursing
sections.summary: Community Health Posts grew to around 150, Community Nursing team areas will expand from 18 to 29, and MOH and MND plan a senior housing pilot.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To support preventive health, we grew the number of Community Health Posts to around 150.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will now expand the number of areas covered by Community Nursing teams from 18 to 29 areas around Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will also partner more Senior Centres to make community nursing services accessible to more seniors by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOH and the Ministry of National Development (MND) plan to launch a pilot where seniors buy a home bundled with a package of programmes and services that can be customised to suit their needs and preferences.

sections.label: Community outreach teams reach people
sections.summary: Thirty-nine community outreach teams have been set up and have reached out to over 210,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Thirty-nine community outreach teams have been set up and have reached out to over 210,000 people.

sections.label: Dementia Friends Mobile App sign-ups
sections.summary: The Dementia Friends Mobile App has encouraged over 4,100 people to sign up and assisted over 50 persons since its October 2018 launch.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Our Dementia Friends Mobile App has encouraged more than 4,100 people to sign up as Dementia Friends and assisted over 50 persons since its launch in October 2018.

sections.label: Mental health and dementia services
sections.summary: Access to mental health and dementia services increased in 12 polyclinics, up from eight in 2018, and over 190 GPs were trained as of December 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To strengthen care and support in the community, we increased access to mental health and dementia services in 12 polyclinics, up from eight in 2018 and also at our GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As of December 2018, over 190 GPs have been trained to diagnose and support persons with mental health conditions.

sections.label: MGP benefits in two tranches
sections.summary: Most MGP benefits come in two tranches in July and November 2019, with MediSave accounts automatically credited a first $200 top-up yearly until 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The bulk of the MGP benefits will be available in two tranches, in July and November 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: One, their MediSave accounts will be automatically credited with their first $200 top-up, which they will continue to get once every year until 2023.

sections.label: MG seniors polyclinic subsidy
sections.summary: From 1 November 2019, MG seniors visiting polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics automatically receive an additional 25% off subsidised bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: When MG seniors visit polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics from 1 November 2019 onwards, they will automatically receive an additional 25% off their subsidised bills.

sections.label: Subsidised HPV vaccination programme
sections.summary: MOH will offer fully subsidised HPV vaccination from April 2019 in the national school-based health programme, including Secondary 1 female students and a catch-up programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To bring about more comprehensive coverage of HPV vaccination for cervical cancer prevention, MOH will offer fully subsidised HPV vaccination from April 2019 as part of our national school-based health programme similar to countries, such as the United Kingdom and Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Current and future cohorts of Secondary 1 female students will be offered the HPV vaccination, and a one-time catch-up programme will be progressively provided for current cohorts of secondary school female students.

sections.label: HPV screening test for women
sections.summary: For women aged 30 and above, a more accurate HPV screening test for cervical cancer is introduced, needed every five years instead of Pap smear every three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For women aged 30 and above, we are introducing a more accurate HPV screening test for cervical cancer, which only needs to be done every five years, compared to the current recommended protocol involving Pap smear test which needs to be done once every three years.

sections.label: IVF insurance requirement lifted
sections.summary: The requirement to purchase Assisted Reproduction Programme insurance for women intending to enrol in in vitro fertilisation will be lifted from 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For women intending to enrol in in vitro fertilisation, Mr Louis Ng will be pleased to know that we will lift the requirement for purchase of Assisted Reproduction Programme insurance from 1 April 2019.

sections.label: National Nursing Academy setup
sections.summary: The National Nursing Academy will be set up to coordinate and support lifelong learning across healthcare institutions, schools and training providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Assuring our staff of continued opportunities for professional development is key to retaining them in the healthcare workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will set up the National Nursing Academy (NNA) to coordinate and support lifelong learning across healthcare institutions, schools and training providers.

sections.label: NNA nurse skills frameworks
sections.summary: The NNA will accredit workplace-based training, recognise nurses' skills and competencies, and develop frameworks starting with Community Nursing, then palliative and gerontology care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The NNA will accredit and strengthen the quality of workplace-based training and develop a system to recognise the skills and competencies attained by a nurse at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This will make the skills portable and stackable to advance nurses’ careers and professional practice across healthcare institutions and settings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To facilitate this, NNA will articulate the skills and competencies needed for nurses' evolving roles as part of the larger Skills Framework for Healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will deepen this framework, starting with the Community Nursing Competency Framework, which will be completed by May this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This will be followed by frameworks for palliative and gerontology care in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NNA’s efforts will benefit all nurses and healthcare providers in the public, private and community sectors.

sections.label: Preventive healthcare and CHAS expansion
sections.summary: Preventive healthcare must be expanded urgently, and CHAS is now expanded to subsidise all Singaporeans for chronic disease treatment at private clinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Preventive healthcare has to be expanded quickly and urgently, as the success of which will allow people to live healthily and happily, and will cushion the demand for increasing healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: I am glad that the Minister for Finance has announced that CHAS is now expanded to subsidise all Singaporeans in seeking treatment for chronic diseases at private clinics.

sections.label: Singaporeans' sugar intake
sections.summary: Singaporeans' sugar intake rose from 59 gm a day in 2010 to 60 gm last year, while WHO ideally recommends 25 gm daily.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Singaporeans' sugar intake increased from 59 grammes (gm) a day in 2010 to 60 gm last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a daily sugar intake of 25 gm ideally.

sections.label: NTWU canteens brown rice
sections.summary: 43 NTWU canteens offer healthier brown rice meal options, with SBST contributing $150,000 as an employer to support the initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Today, 43 NTWU canteens offer healthier brown rice meal options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: As an employer, SBST has contributed $150,000 to support this initiative.

sections.label: Tobacco measures and menthol ban
sections.summary: MOH introduced tobacco measures including excise taxes, smoking area restrictions, point-of-sale display ban and higher minimum legal age, and is asked to reconsider banning flavored and menthol cigarettes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Chairman, MOH has introduced a series of tobacco measures to make it harder for smokers and to deter new ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: These include excise taxes, restrictions on smoking areas, a ban on point-of-sale display and a gradual increase in the minimum legal age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Very soon, cigarette packaging will also have to be plain and standardised, with bigger graphic health warnings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Can the Ministry take one step further and reconsider a ban on flavored and, particularly, menthol cigarettes, such as what Canada has recently done and which the US is considering once again?

sections.label: Minimum legal age and tobacco tax
sections.summary: It is asked whether the minimum legal age should be increased beyond 21 and whether tobacco tax is sufficiently prohibitive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: For example, should we increase the minimum legal age beyond 21 and is our tobacco tax sufficiently prohibitive?

sections.label: Polyclinic network expansion
sections.summary: MOH plans to enlarge the polyclinic network from 20 to about 30 to 32 by 2030, with two more polyclinics in Serangoon and Tengah expected operational by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: MOH had previously announced plans to enlarge our polyclinic network from 20 currently to about 30 to 32 polyclinics by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Currently, these are slated for Bukit Panjang, Eunos, Kallang, Sembawang, Khatib and Tampines North.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Members that in addition to these, two more polyclinics will be developed in Serangoon and Tengah, which are expected to be operational by 2025.

sections.label: GP clinics in PCN scheme
sections.summary: More than 300 GP clinics formed 10 PCNs serving over 70,000 chronic disease patients, with over 450 clinics participating this year and a 2020 target.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Last year, more than 300 GP clinics participated in this scheme to form 10 PCNs and collectively are serving more than 70,000 patients with chronic disease.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To date, more than 5,000 patients with diabetes have benefited from this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This year, there are more than 450 GP clinics participating in the PCN scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In order to benefit more patients with chronic disease, MOH targets to have half of all CHAS GP clinics participating in the PCN scheme by 2020.

sections.label: HealthHub introductory diabetes materials
sections.summary: A beta version of the introductory section for newly diagnosed patients has been on HealthHub since December 2018, with full materials in four languages due in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: A beta version of the introductory section, which is mainly targeted at newly diagnosed patients, has been available on HealthHub since December 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The full set of materials will be published on HealthHub in four languages in the second half of 2019.

sections.label: National Diabetic Foot Workgroup framework
sections.summary: MOH formed the National Diabetic Foot Workgroup in April last year, recommending a risk-stratified diabetic foot framework to be launched from the second quarter of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: MOH formed the National Diabetic Foot Workgroup in April last year to develop a strategy to reduce such amputations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: A key recommendation of the Workgroup is a risk-stratified diabetic foot screening, management and escalation framework, which aims to streamline diabetic foot care services across primary and tertiary care, and provide healthcare professionals with clinical guidelines for timely and appropriate care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This framework will be progressively launched in our polyclinics and public hospitals from the second quarter of 2019.

sections.label: Generic drug usage by volume
sections.summary: By volume, usage of generic drugs in the basket rose from 87% in 2013 to 99% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: By volume, the usage of the generic drugs in the basket has increased from 87% in 2013 to 99% in 2017.

sections.label: Fee benchmarks for surgical procedures
sections.summary: Fee benchmarks for professional fees for common surgical procedures were introduced in November last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As shared by Minister Gan Kim Yong earlier, we have since introduced fee benchmarks in November last year for professional fees for common surgical procedures.

sections.label: Co-payment for new IP riders
sections.summary: All new IP riders are required to have a co-payment of 5% or more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: All new IP riders are required to have a co-payment of 5% or more.

sections.label: Children with Leukaemia treatment
sections.summary: About 240 Singaporean and PR children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia received personalised treatment over the past 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For example, approximately 240 Singaporean and PR children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia have benefited from personalised treatment in the past 15 years.

sections.label: Infectious Diseases Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Infectious Diseases (Amendment) Bill was passed in January 2019 and will come into effect in the subsequent months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The Infectious Diseases (Amendment) Bill was passed in January 2019 and will come into effect in the subsequent months.

sections.label: MediSave influenza vaccinations increase
sections.summary: MediSave used for influenza vaccinations rose about 60%, from about 32,000 to about 52,000 a year later.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For example, MediSave used for influenza vaccinations has increased by about 60%, from about 32,000 between November 2016 and October 2017, to about 52,000 in the same period a year later.

sections.label: NCID training and research
sections.summary: NCID will conduct training and research to strengthen national preparedness against outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: NCID will also conduct training and research to strengthen national preparedness against outbreaks.

sections.label: Means-tested healthcare subsidies
sections.summary: The Government provides means-tested subsidies of up to 80% for Singaporeans across all public healthcare settings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the Government provides means-tested subsidies of up to 80% for Singaporeans across all public healthcare settings.

sections.label: Subsidised hospitalisation cash payments
sections.summary: Seven in 10 subsidised hospitalisations needed no cash payment, and eight in 10 paid under $100 in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Seven in 10 subsidised hospitalisations by Singaporeans did not require any cash payment, and eight in 10 paid less than $100 in cash after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

sections.label: CHAS extension to all Singaporeans
sections.summary: CHAS will be extended to cover all Singaporeans with chronic conditions, as mentioned by the Prime Minister at the National Day Rally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the Prime Minister at the National Day Rally last year, we will extend CHAS to cover all Singaporeans with chronic conditions.

sections.label: Household income and annual subsidies
sections.summary: This covers households with per capita household income above $1,800 and provides up to $160 of annual subsidies for chronic conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This would consist of households with a per capita household income (PCHI) greater than $1,800.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It will provide up to $160 of annual subsidies for chronic conditions.

sections.label: CHAS subsidy payout amount
sections.summary: More than $200 million a year is expected to be paid out on CHAS subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Collectively, we expect to pay out more than $200 million a year on CHAS subsidies.

sections.label: Means-tested subsidies, CareShield Life, MediSave
sections.summary: About two-thirds of households qualify for means-tested subsidies up to 80% for intermediate and long-term care, and CareShield Life will provide at least $600 monthly for the severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Today, around two-thirds of households qualify for means-tested subsidies of up to 80% for intermediate and long-term care services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will be introducing CareShield Life, which provides a payout of at least $600 per month for persons who are severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Severely disabled individuals with $20,000 balance in their MediSave, can expect to withdraw MediSave up to about 70 months, after setting aside a minimum of $5,000, taking into account other MediSave uses, such as paying for medical expenses.

sections.label: MediShield Life pregnancy complications review
sections.summary: MOH would review extending MediShield Life to cover serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications, as mentioned last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To alleviate the concerns over healthcare expenses related to marriage and parenthood aspirations, we mentioned last year that MOH would review how to extend MediShield Life to cover serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications.

sections.label: MediShield Life pregnancy complication coverage
sections.summary: From 1 April, MediShield Life covers inpatient treatments for serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications under existing inpatient claim limits, potentially benefiting up to 4,000 patients yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: From 1 April this year, MediShield Life will cover inpatient treatments for serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications, such as eclampsia, cervical incompetency and postpartum haemorrhage, under the existing inpatient claim limits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There are a few more of such complications which will also be covered, and the full list will be found on the MOH website.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This enhancement can potentially benefit up to 4,000 patients each year.

sections.label: MediShield Life bone marrow transplant coverage
sections.summary: MediShield Life will cover outpatient bone marrow transplant costs up to $6,000 per treatment at approved hospitals from 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To better support these patients in continuing their bone marrow transplant treatments in the outpatient setting, MediShield Life will be extended to cover these costs up to a claim limit of $6,000 per treatment at approved hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This will apply to treatments performed on or after 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This enhancement can potentially benefit over 20 patients a year.

sections.label: 2017 actual claims versus expected
sections.summary: In 2017, actual claims amounted to 99% of expected claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2017, for example, our actual claims amounted to 99% of expected claims.

sections.label: MediShield Life Fund incurred loss ratio
sections.summary: The MediShield Life Fund's incurred loss ratio over the last five years was about 97%, ensuring sustainability without being excessive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The incurred loss ratio of the MediShield Life Fund over the last five years was approximately 97%, sufficient to ensure the sustainability of the scheme but not excessive.

sections.label: New Home Caregiving Grant
sections.summary: A new Home Caregiving Grant by end 2019 replaces the Foreign Domestic Worker Grant with an enhanced $200 monthly quantum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, we will be introducing a new Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) by end 2019 as further financial support to care recipients living in the community with permanent disability and require some assistance in at least three ADLs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The HCG replaces the existing Foreign Domestic Worker (FDW) Grant with an enhanced quantum of $200 per month.

sections.label: Respite services and night respite pilot
sections.summary: Over 2,400 clients have benefited from respite services, and a night respite pilot with selected nursing homes starts in second half of 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To date, over 2,400 clients have benefited from these respite services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will be piloting a new night respite service with selected nursing home providers in the second half of 2019 to support caregivers of seniors with dementia who experience behavioural and sleep difficulties at night.

sections.label: Proposed Healthcare Services Bill aims
sections.summary: The proposed Healthcare Services Bill aims to enhance regulatory clarity, strengthen licensee governance, safeguard patient safety and welfare, and ensure continuity of care and accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The proposed Healthcare Services Bill, which will come before Parliament shortly, aims to enhance the regulatory clarity as to the types of healthcare services regulated, strengthen the governance of the licensees providing the healthcare services, provide the necessary safeguards to patient safety and welfare, and to ensure continuity of care and accountability.

sections.label: Productivity savings in healthcare
sections.summary: Productivity efforts saved about 300,000 manhours yearly across public healthcare and community care institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On average, our productivity efforts have saved about 300,000 manhours across public healthcare and community care institutions per year.

sections.label: Trans fat and PHO ban
sections.summary: Local trans fat halved from 2010 to 2018, and a ban on partially-hydrogenated oil will extend to prepackaged food products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Local trans fat halved from about two grammes per day in 2010 to one gramme per day in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We will be introducing a ban on partially-hydrogenated oil (PHO) in our food.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Current trans fat regulations only apply to fats and oil.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: This ban will also extend to prepackaged food products, such as snacks, baked foods, prepared meals and fat spread.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence target 2020
sections.summary: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about helping smokers quit, and a target of under 10% smoking prevalence by 2020 was announced in May 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about efforts to help smokers quit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: I had announced in May 2018 that we are working towards a smoking prevalence of less than 10% by 2020.

sections.label: Student smoking rate drop
sections.summary: Smoking rate among secondary school, ITE and polytechnic students dropped from 8% in 2011-2013 to about 4% in 2014-2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Smoking rate among secondary school, ITE and polytechnic students dropped from 8% in 2011-2013 to about to 4% in 2014-2016.

sections.label: Tobacco retail licence actions
sections.summary: In 2018, HSA suspended tobacco retail licences of 23 first-time offenders and revoked four repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In 2018, HSA suspended the tobacco retail licences of 23 first-time offender retailers and revoked four repeat offenders.

sections.label: Allied Health degree intake increase
sections.summary: MOH worked with MOE and SIT to raise intake of four Allied Health degree programmes from 230 in 2016 to about 300 students in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: MOH had worked with MOE and SIT to increase the intake of four Allied Health degree programmes in Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Diagnostic Radiography and Radiation Therapy from 230 in 2016 to about 300 students in 2018.

sections.label: Allied health skills framework
sections.summary: A Skills Framework for Healthcare is launched for six professions, covering nurses, pharmacy technicians, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, speech therapists and patient service associates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about continuing development and career progression for allied health professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We are launching the "Skills Framework for Healthcare" for six professions – Nurses, Pharmacy Technicians, Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists, Speech Therapists and Patient Service Associates.

sections.label: TCM practitioner funding
sections.summary: As of end 2018, more than $70,000 had been given to over 400 TCM practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: As of end 2018, we had given more than $70,000 to over 400 TCM practitioners.

sections.label: Subsidised CHAS health checks
sections.summary: From May 2019, subsidised blood sugar and cholesterol checks at CHAS clinics do not require overnight or 12-hour fasting.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: From May 2019, you can have subsidised checks for blood sugar and cholesterol levels at CHAS clinics without having to fast overnight or for 12 hours.

sections.label: Healthier meals consumed 2018
sections.summary: Singaporeans consumed 131 million healthier meals in 2018, double the number in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Singaporeans consumed 131 million healthier meals in 2018, double that in 2017.

sections.label: Halal Healthier Choice dishes
sections.summary: Halal Healthier Choice dishes at hawker centres rose from two in 2017, thosai and mee soto, to six now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In 2017, there were only two halal Healthier Choice dishes at the hawker centres, namely, thosai and mee soto.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Now, there are more choices with six halal dishes that are healthier.

sections.label: Halal healthier food options
sections.summary: Malay restaurants, 1,100 food establishments, 107 caterers and 24 Malay wedding caterers now serve healthier halal dishes and food.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Well-known Malay restaurants also began to serve a wider choice of delicious and healthy food, such as Rumah Minang, Hajah Maimunah, Sabar Menanti and many more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: These are some of the 1,100 food establishments that serve healthier halal dishes using brown rice, healthier cooking oil, vegetables and less coconut milk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: If you attend religious feasts or weddings, healthier choices are also available.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: There are now 107 caterers providing halal healthy food, including 24 Malay wedding caterers like Jamil Catering and Istana Wedding Services.

sections.label: Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah programme
sections.summary: The JKJU programme began with five mosques, expanded to 23 mosques, and benefited more than 4,500 congregants this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The "Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah (JKJU)" or Taking Care of Health, Taking Care of Community programme launched two years ago began with five mosques.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: It has expanded to include 23 mosques, with various exercise programmes, health workshops and health screening sessions held at JKJU mosques, and it has benefited more than 4,500 congregants this year.

sections.label: 24-week abortion cut-off
sections.summary: The current 24 gestational week cut-off for abortion was based on scientific evidence of foetal viability outside the womb.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In response to the cut, the current cut-off of 24 gestational weeks for abortion was based on scientific evidence of foetal viability outside the womb.

sections.label: Abortions at 22 to 24 weeks
sections.summary: In 2018, about 1% of abortions were performed between 22 and 24 gestational weeks, over half due to foetal anomalies and other medical reasons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In addition, in 2018, it is worthwhile to note that about 1% of all abortions performed were performed between 22 and 24 gestational weeks, of which more than half of these abortions were performed due to foetal anomalies and other medical reasons.

sections.label: Published drug and medical technology guidances
sections.summary: They have published almost 33 drug guidances and three medical technology guidances as of 2 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In fact, they have published almost 33 drug guidances, three medical technology guidances, as of 2 January 2019.

sections.label: MediShield Life payout appeals
sections.summary: They do not look at appeals for MediShield Life payouts, but can consider appeals for higher MediSave withdrawals or MediFund use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At this point in time, we do not look at appeals for MediShield Life payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The reason for that, obviously, is the more you get the payout on an individual, that compromises the fund because you draw out from the other persons who have put premiums inside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But on Dr Chia Shi-Lu's point, we can consider appeals for higher MediSave withdrawals or, if not, then the use of MediFund in the meantime.

sections.label: Bringing together clusters' supply chain functions
sections.summary: The idea is to bring together supply chain functions of all clusters to achieve economies of scale and aggregate demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The idea is to bring together the supply chain functions of all our clusters so that we can achieve economies of scale, aggregate demand and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The first step is to better understand the procurement practices of the different clusters and see whether we can harmonise them, first, to achieve economies of scale by aggregating the purchases of the various clusters, and then we have a higher leverage with our suppliers so that we can negotiate for better pricing.

sections.label: Private ambulance fee transparency
sections.summary: The Healthcare Services Bill will regulate private ambulances and mandate publication of common fees and bill components for consumer transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Healthcare Services Bill that I talked about will regulate private ambulances, and Ms Sylvia Lim, in particular, spoke about the publication of rates for more transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That legislation will mandate the publication of common fees charged as well as give more transparency to the bill components to be paid by the consumers so that they will know upfront what those costs would be.

sections.label: Allied health care models study
sections.summary: MOH is studying care models to help patients access allied health services earlier, such as direct referral to community physiotherapists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: MOH is actually currently studying the models of care that will help patients access allied health services earlier, say, for example, the direct referral to community physiotherapists for agreed musculoskeletal presentations.

sections.label: Daycare and homecare places added
sections.summary: 2,700 daycare and 2,300 homecare places were added since 2015, with national capacity sufficient though local imbalances may exist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, we have added 2,700 daycare places since 2015 so that seniors can access daycare services near their homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have also added another 2,300 homecare places over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We see sufficient capacity at the national level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, in fact, at the national level, there are more vacancies than waitlisted seniors, except that there could be an imbalance in demand and supply within certain local areas because of patient or family preferences and so on.

sections.label: Value-driven care conditions
sections.summary: 17 conditions have been initiated under value-driven care, with plans to expand this over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To date, we have initiated a total of 17 conditions under value-driven care, and we want to expand this over time.
